In Jetty 12 this nested type is an accumulator/holder that collects suppressed throwables and rethrows them (e.g. via an ifExceptionThrow-style method) rather than being itself throwable, so the flagged property really is present, and the name genuinely invites readers to assume it can be thrown or caught "MultiException". The consequence stated \u2014 confusion for users of the class \u2014 follows directly and is not ruled out by anything in the warning; it is a naming/readability concern rather than a behavioural defect. I would have had to check the class declaration line to confirm it has no Throwable supertype, but the tool inspects exactly that.
runs.issue_signature: class named as an exception without extending throwable
runs.developer_explanation: This nested helper class is named as if it were an exception type, but it does not extend Exception or Throwable \u2014 it is a container that collects failures and rethrows them. Readers and IDE users will reasonably expect to be able to throw or catch it, which they cannot, and the name collides conceptually with the older throwable class of the same name. Consider renaming it to something like ExceptionCollector or MultiCause, or documenting clearly that it is a collector rather than a throwable.

findings.message: Class implements Cloneable but does not define or use clone method

runs.reasoning: The warning's claim is a purely structural fact derived from the bytecode: the class declares Cloneable yet neither overrides nor calls clone(), and SpotBugs reads this directly from the class file, so the claim is almost certainly materially correct. In Jetty, LazyList is a static utility holder (private constructor, all-static helpers) that historically declared `implements Cloneable, Serializable`, which makes the marker interface meaningless and misleading to callers who may assume the class supports cloning. To be fully certain I would have had to read the class declaration and check for any clone() override or internal super.clone() call. The declaration is dead/misleading API surface rather than a wrong result, so it is a maintainability issue.
runs.issue_signature: class declares Cloneable without defining or using clone
runs.developer_explanation: This class advertises that it can be cloned by declaring Cloneable, but it never overrides clone(), so the inherited protected Object.clone() is all that exists and callers cannot actually clone it in any meaningful way. For a class made up of static helpers this marker interface is simply misleading. Either drop the Cloneable declaration or provide a proper public clone() implementation.

findings.message: Comparator doesn't implement Serializable

runs.reasoning: The warning's claim is purely structural: the class implements Comparator but not Serializable, which the description itself frames as a defensive-programming consideration rather than an actual failure. That structural fact is almost certainly accurate as reported, so the claim is materially correct. The stated consequence is explicitly conditional ("if a comparator is used to construct an ordered collection such as a TreeMap"), so it is not contradicted even if this comparator is only used for an in-memory list sort. To be fully certain I would have to check whether the comparator is a non-static inner class capturing non-serializable state, which would make adding Serializable misleading rather than helpful, but that would affect the remedy, not the correctness of the claim.
runs.issue_signature: comparator implementation not marked serializable
runs.developer_explanation: This comparator class does not implement Serializable. If it is ever handed to a TreeMap, TreeSet or similar ordered collection that later needs to be serialized, the serialization will fail because the comparator is part of the collection's state. Since comparators usually carry little or no state, adding Serializable (and, if it is an inner class, making it static) is a cheap safeguard; if the comparator captures non-serializable state and is only ever used for a local list sort, you can document that instead.
